// The helper layer of the reach fixture: every spawn lives here, two packages
// away from the command that reaches it, so an edge set that stopped at package
// boundaries would report all of them as reachable from nothing.
//
// A fixture, not compiled source — see ungated.go.txt for why .go.txt.

package helperpkg

import "os/exec"

// HopOne -> hopTwo -> a spawn. Two NAMED hops, neither of them the command.
func HopOne() error { return hopTwo() }

func hopTwo() error {
	return exec.Command("git", "log", "--oneline").Run()
}

// GatedOnly reaches its spawn through a package-level var seam, which is how
// this codebase makes a subprocess substitutable in tests.
func GatedOnly() error { return runFn() }

var runFn = doSpawn

func doSpawn() error {
	return exec.Command("go", "test", "./...").Run()
}

// Shared is reached by BOTH commands, which is the mixed class: a marker is
// required, and the finding for an unmarked one names the ungated reach.
func Shared() error { return sharedSpawn() }

func sharedSpawn() error {
	return exec.Command("rsync", "-a", "src", "dst").Run()
}

// Displayed is reached only by the command that reads consent without acting
// on it, so it is ungated however the name rule is written.
func Displayed() error {
	return exec.Command("markdownlint", "docs").Run()
}

// Orphan is reached by no command at all. Fail-closed: an unresolvable or
// absent path must read as "no gate covers this", never as "nothing to do".
func Orphan() error {
	return exec.Command("cargo", "build").Run()
}

// LaneConsented is the name-rule bait: a caller that discards its verdict must
// not be counted as gating just because the identifier ends in "Consented".
func LaneConsented() (int, error) { return 0, nil }
